domain_label: Plated-Jewelry Social Polling — Incentive Bias, Self-Selection & Platform Sampling Error, Sample-Size Reasoning, and US Giveaway/Disclosure Law
purpose: A method for turning a paid IG/TikTok category poll of ~18-25 US women into an honestly-caveated preference signal by naming how a 'get something free' incentive biases responses [FACT], how self-selection and algorithmic platform delivery bias the sampling frame [FACT], how much sample is the minimum to read any signal [METHOD], how to read noisy overlapping poll numbers without over-claiming a winner [METHOD], and how to stay inside the US FTC endorsement/disclosure rules and sweepstakes/promotion law and the IG/TikTok promotion guidelines [FACT] — never inventing the audience composition, response-lift, or category-preference numbers the poll exists to measure.
assumptions: the poll's job is to rank a small set of jewelry categories (earrings / necklaces / rings / bracelets / anklets) for the launch-set decision, not to size the market; it yields a preference signal, not a market truth [FACT-scope]

the target population is US women roughly 18-25 who would buy fashion/plated jewelry, while the reachable sampling frame is whoever IG/TikTok's ad algorithm delivers the poll to and who chooses to respond; the two are not the same set [FACT-survey methodology]

survey-methodology facts are cited as established: voluntary-response/self-selection bias, nonresponse bias, coverage bias, satisficing/straightlining, demand characteristics, and the Total-Survey-Error framework (Groves et al.) [FACT]; margin-of-error arithmetic for a proportion is standard [FACT]

US promotion law is cited as fact but not as legal advice: a promotion with consideration + chance + prize is an illegal lottery, so a compliant giveaway removes consideration via 'No Purchase Necessary' + an equal-dignity Alternative Method of Entry (AMOE); NY/FL require registration + bonding for prize pools over $5,000 [FACT]; the FTC Endorsement Guides (16 CFR Part 255, revised 2023) require disclosure of material connections including incentives [FACT]

platform promotion guidelines (Meta/Instagram, TikTok) are real but change over time, so they are cited as [FACT-as-of] with the standing obligation to re-verify the live guideline before launch, never hardened as permanent

every measured quantity the owner wants (how many respond, response-lift from the incentive, the true category ranking, the actual audience age/gender/buyer mix) is left as [METHOD] to measure or [UNKNOWN]; no audience percentage, lift figure, or preference share is invented as fact
exclusions: poll/survey instrument wording, question-type choice (single-choice vs MaxDiff/ranked), option ordering and leading-question avoidance (that is kb1_instrument_design; this KB assumes a designed instrument and governs its sampling, incentive and reading)

the paid-ad mechanics themselves — audience targeting setup, campaign objective, creative, cost-per-response and bidding (that is kb3_paid_reach_and_signal; this KB governs the bias and legal envelope around them)
the downstream assortment/SKU-ranking decision that consumes the signal (that is the S5 assortment specialist; this KB stops at a caveated ranked signal + confidence)
market sizing, demographic purchase rates, brand share and price — the S1 market specialist's public-data methods; this KB never emits a market number
actual legal/tax filing advice for a specific sweepstakes; this models the compliance envelope and its decisions, not a filed promotion

glossary.definition: The bias in a sample where respondents choose themselves in: an IG/TikTok poll is answered only by those who saw it, cared, and had a moment, so the opinionated/engaged/available are over-represented and the sample systematically differs from the target population; crucially this bias does not shrink as sample size grows [FACT-survey methodology].

The coverage/selection bias introduced by IG/TikTok delivering the poll to an engagement- or conversion-optimized (often lookalike) slice of users rather than a random draw of the target population, so the delivered frame is shaped by the ad algorithm's objective, not by representativeness [FACT].

The systematic distortion an entry-prize creates: it lifts response but pulls in prize-seekers/freebie-hunters, induces demand characteristics (answering to please or to qualify), satisficing/straightlining, and duplicate/bot entries; it changes both who answers (audience-mismatch) and how they answer, and its magnitude on this poll is [UNKNOWN] until measured [FACT-mechanism].

The framework (Groves et al.) that decomposes a survey's error into coverage error, sampling error, nonresponse error and measurement error; it is the organizing lens telling you that a bigger n only reduces sampling error and does nothing for the coverage/nonresponse/measurement errors an incentivized social poll is dominated by [FACT].

For a measured proportion p at confidence z, MoE = z*sqrt(p(1-p)/n); at 95% (z~1.96) and the worst-case p=0.5, n~=384 gives +/-5%, n~=100 gives ~+/-9.8%, n~=1000 gives ~+/-3.1% [FACT-statistics]; it bounds only random sampling error, never the self-selection or incentive bias.

The compliance device that keeps a prize giveaway from being an illegal lottery: a lottery is consideration + chance + prize, so removing consideration via a free, equal-dignity Alternative Method of Entry (e.g. mail-in or free-form entry) and a clear 'No Purchase Necessary' makes it a lawful sweepstakes [FACT-US promotion law].

Under the FTC Endorsement Guides (16 CFR Part 255, revised 2023), any material connection between a brand and a person promoting/entering — including an incentive, prize entry, or free product — must be disclosed clearly and conspicuously (e.g. #ad, 'sweepstakes entry'); the disclosure duty falls on the advertiser to enforce [FACT].

A compliant sweepstakes publishes official rules stating the sponsor, eligibility, start/end dates, free AMOE, odds, prize ARV and winner selection; New York and Florida require registration and a surety bond for prize pools over $5,000, and Rhode Island for retail promotions over $500 [FACT-state law].

Meta/Instagram and TikTok promotion policies that a giveaway must follow — a complete release of the platform, acknowledgment that the promotion is not sponsored/endorsed by it, and a ban on requiring inaccurate tagging or certain share mechanics; these guidelines change, so they are [FACT-as-of] and must be re-verified live before launch.

The explicit decision rule that converts a poll read into act / re-run / triangulate: it requires the leading category's margin to clear the confidence interval AND the bias direction (incentive + self-selection + nonresponse) not to plausibly account for the lead; a within-margin or bias-explainable lead is 'no decision', not a winner.

nodes.definition: The load-bearing node: model exactly how a 'get something free' incentive biases the poll [FACT-mechanism]. Attaching a prize does two things. (1) It changes HOW people answer: demand characteristics (respondents answer to qualify or to please, not truthfully), satisficing/straightlining (rushing to reach the prize), and acquiescence — all pulling answers toward whatever the respondent thinks 'wins' the freebie. (2) It changes WHO answers: it recruits prize-seekers/freebie-hunters and disproportionately those with time to chase giveaways, plus duplicate and bot entries — a population whose jewelry preference may be uncorrelated with genuine buying intent. The incentive therefore does not merely add noise; it adds SYSTEMATIC bias in a direction (toward the prize-relevant option and toward non-buyer respondents) and amplifies the self-selection bias already present. nodes.definition: Give the minimum-signal sample-size reasoning [METHOD], honestly bounded. For a measured proportion p the margin of error is MoE = z*sqrt(p(1-p)/n); at 95% confidence (z~1.96) and worst-case p=0.5, n~=384 yields +/-5%, n~=100 yields ~+/-9.8%, n~=1000 yields ~+/-3.1% [FACT-statistics]. The decisive caveat, inherited from TOTAL_SURVEY_ERROR: this formula bounds ONLY random sampling error under a random sample; it does not and cannot bound the self-selection, platform-coverage or incentive bias, so a tight MoE on a biased sample is precision without accuracy. n is a floor to read a signal, never a fix for bias.

nodes.definition: State what weighting can and cannot recover [METHOD]. Post-stratification/quota weighting reweights the responding sample so its measured demographics (age, gender, geo) match the target population's known marginals — partially correcting the coverage/nonresponse skew the nonresponse analysis measured. Its hard limits, stated honestly: (1) it can only weight on axes you MEASURED for respondents and KNOW for the target; (2) it cannot conjure respondents from a group with zero coverage (no 18-22 respondents => no weight fixes their absence); (3) it does nothing for the self-selection axis that is unmeasured (e.g. 'is a freebie-hunter'), which is exactly the incentive's worst bias; and (4) heavy weights on thin cells explode variance, so a few respondents standing in for a large target group produce an unstable estimate. nodes.definition: State the discipline for reading the numbers honestly [METHOD]. nodes.definition: State the US FTC disclosure obligation as fact [FACT-16 CFR Part 255, Endorsement Guides, revised June 2023]. nodes.definition: State the US sweepstakes/promotion-law envelope as fact [FACT-US promotion law]. A promotion that combines all three of CONSIDERATION (something of value given to enter), CHANCE (winner picked randomly) and PRIZE is an illegal private LOTTERY. A giveaway is kept lawful by removing one element — for a chance-based draw, remove consideration via a clear 'No Purchase Necessary' AND a free, EQUAL-DIGNITY Alternative Method of Entry (AMOE) giving non-buyers the same odds (e.g. a free mail-in or web entry). A compliant sweepstakes publishes OFFICIAL RULES stating sponsor, eligibility (US, age, exclusions), start/end dates, free AMOE, odds, prize description + approximate retail value (ARV), and winner selection/notification. Registration and a surety BOND are required for prize pools over $5,000 in New York and Florida (and Rhode Island for retail promotions over $500). A skill-based CONTEST removes chance instead and has different rules. This is the compliance structure the owner's 'get free to enter' idea must be built inside; it is [FACT] law, not legal advice for a specific filing.

nodes.definition: State the privacy, consent and ethics obligations of collecting entries/emails from a young audience [FACT]. conflict_axes.name: engagement_optimized_delivery_vs_representative_delivery
conflict_axes.description: Optimizing the ad for cheap engagement reaches responses fastest but delivers the least representative slice; representative delivery costs more and yields fewer responses.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: target the buyer segment and read the delivered-audience stats, accepting higher cost-per-response for a frame closer to the target

conflict_axes.name: legal_compliance_cost_vs_promotion_simplicity
conflict_axes.description: A fully compliant sweepstakes (AMOE, official rules, FTC disclosure, state registration, privacy consent) adds friction and cost; a simple 'tag to win' is easier but risks an illegal lottery, FTC and platform violations.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: always build inside the compliance envelope; the illegal-lottery/FTC/platform exposure of a simple giveaway outweighs its convenience

conflict_axes.name: act_now_on_poll_vs_triangulate_first
conflict_axes.description: The owner wants to move fast on the poll result while the honest state may be that the biased signal must be triangulated with S1 public-data and existing on-site data before acting.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: act only when the validity gate's three conditions all hold; otherwise triangulate with S1/on-site data rather than act on a weak biased poll

conflict_axes.name: measured_fact_vs_desired_number
conflict_axes.description: The owner wants concrete audience, lift and preference numbers, but those are exactly the [UNKNOWN]s the poll exists to measure and must not be pre-invented as facts.
poles: hold the number as [UNKNOWN] until measured
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: keep audience-composition, lift, fraud-rate and true-preference numbers in the [UNKNOWN]/[ESTIMATE] registers with method, never promoted to [FACT]

edge_cases.description: A generic high-value cash prize floods the poll with freebie-hunters whose jewelry preference is uncorrelated with buying intent, producing a large confident dataset about the wrong people
edge_cases.trigger: a broad, generic, high-value prize broadcast for maximum entries
edge_cases.mitigation: use a buyer-relevant jewelry prize, target the 18-25 buyer segment, and check the responder profile against the target before trusting the ranking

edge_cases.description: A 'tag two friends and share to enter' mechanic makes a platform action the only way to enter, creating an illegal lottery (consideration + chance + prize) and breaching platform tagging rules
edge_cases.trigger: an entry requires a purchase or a mandatory platform action with no free equal-dignity AMOE
edge_cases.mitigation: add a free equal-dignity AMOE and 'No Purchase Necessary', and drop mechanics the platform prohibits

edge_cases.description: The prize/incentive is not disclosed, so the incentivized poll ad and entry posts violate the FTC material-connection rule
edge_cases.trigger: a giveaway-tied poll runs without a clear-and-conspicuous disclosure
edge_cases.mitigation: add a clear plain-language disclosure ('sweepstakes entry') that the advertiser enforces, not buried in a hashtag block

edge_cases.description: A within-margin 41%-39% top-two split is reported as 'earrings win' and drives the launch set, when the intervals overlap and the incentive skew could produce the gap
edge_cases.trigger: a within-margin lead is read as a decision
edge_cases.mitigation: call overlapping intervals 'no decision', get more responses or triangulate, and never act on a bias-explainable lead

edge_cases.description: The team celebrates '5,000 responses' as proof of a reliable poll while coverage, nonresponse and incentive bias are untouched by the large n
edge_cases.trigger: raw response count is cited as evidence of representativeness
edge_cases.mitigation: state that only sampling error shrinks with n and budget effort on the non-n-fixable coverage/nonresponse/incentive biases

edge_cases.description: A 5-option poll is sized on total n so each option's cell (~n/5) is too thin to separate the middle options
edge_cases.trigger: sample sized on the total rather than per-option cell counts
edge_cases.mitigation: size for per-option precision (each option's count, not the total, sets its margin) or reduce the option count

edge_cases.description: Weighting up a single 18-year-old respondent to represent all 18-22 buyers produces a wildly unstable estimate presented as representative
edge_cases.trigger: post-stratification weighting on a thin or near-zero-coverage cell
edge_cases.mitigation: refuse to weight thin/zero-coverage cells, report the coverage gap honestly, and do not certify the sample as representative

edge_cases.description: A prize value rises and giveaway-farm bots block-vote one category via duplicate/multi-account entries, moving the ranking
edge_cases.trigger: a higher-value prize with no deduplication or attention checks
edge_cases.mitigation: deduplicate on account/device, add attention checks and geo/age eligibility, and separate the entry act from the counted preference

edge_cases.description: Entry emails are collected and later used for marketing with no notice, opt-out, or age gate, breaching CCPA/CAN-SPAM and risking COPPA if under-13s were reached
edge_cases.trigger: email/handle collection without consent, notice, opt-out, or age gate
edge_cases.mitigation: add notice-at-collection, opt-out, data minimization and a US age gate, and use data only as disclosed

edge_cases.description: A prize-relevant question ('answer to win these earrings') pulls respondents to over-pick the prize category via demand characteristics, inflating that option's share
edge_cases.trigger: the prize is tied to or aligned with a specific answer option
edge_cases.mitigation: decouple the prize from the answer (entry independent of which option is chosen) and say so, then discount any prize-aligned option

edge_cases.description: A stale copy of the Meta/TikTok promotion guideline is relied on and a now-prohibited share/tag mechanic gets the giveaway taken down
edge_cases.trigger: using a previously-allowed platform mechanic without re-verifying the live guideline
edge_cases.mitigation: re-verify the live platform promotion guideline immediately before launch and treat cited details as [FACT-as-of]

edge_cases.description: The poll's biased category ranking is passed to assortment as a clean winner, stripped of its caveats and decision-state, and drives a false SKU commitment
edge_cases.trigger: a point winner is handed off without bias caveats or the act/re-run/triangulate state
edge_cases.mitigation: hand off the ranking as a caveated range with the decision-state, bias caveats and legal status, stopping before the SKU choice

workflow.action: Fix the poll's decision job and target
workflow.description: State the poll as a category-ranking instrument for the six-item launch set, target US women ~18-25, with a 'separate the top categories' good-enough bar, not a market-sizing tool
workflow.gate: the ranking job, the ~18-25 target and the good-enough bar are stated, market-sizing excluded

workflow.action: Separate target, frame and responding sample
workflow.description: Name the three populations and the coverage vs nonresponse gaps, flagging frame/sample composition [UNKNOWN] until measured
workflow.gate: target, reachable frame and responding sample are distinguished with the two gaps named

workflow.description: Name coverage/sampling/nonresponse/measurement error and the rule that only sampling error shrinks with n, prioritizing the non-n-fixable errors
workflow.gate: the four error sources and the only-sampling-error-shrinks-with-n rule are stated

workflow.action: Name the self-selection and platform biases
workflow.description: State voluntary-response over-representation of engaged fans and algorithmic coverage skew as non-averaging systematic offsets
workflow.gate: self-selection and platform coverage bias are stated as non-averaging with [UNKNOWN] magnitudes

workflow.description: State how the prize changes how people answer (demand characteristics/satisficing) and who answers (prize-seekers), amplifying self-selection, lift/magnitude [UNKNOWN]
workflow.gate: the how-they-answer and who-answers effects are stated as systematic bias with lift flagged [UNKNOWN]

workflow.description: State the prize decoupling respondents from ~18-25 buyers as the default-to-disprove, and the predictable bot/duplicate fraud with its controls
workflow.gate: buyer-mismatch is set as default-to-disprove and fraud controls (dedup, attention, geo/age) are named

workflow.action: Design the incentive to balance lift and bias
workflow.description: State relevance, draw-vs-guaranteed, decoupling, gating and modest value as levers with an incentivized-vs-not A/B split to measure the tradeoff
workflow.gate: the five levers, the lift-vs-bias tradeoff and the A/B measurement are stated with effects [UNKNOWN]

workflow.action: Set the minimum sample and reading rules
workflow.description: State the MoE formula, the n~=384/+/-5% and per-cell anchors, and that n bounds only sampling error not bias; then the overlapping-CI no-decision reading rule
workflow.gate: the MoE anchors, the per-cell trap and the n-not-a-bias-fix caveat are stated

workflow.action: Estimate nonresponse skew and weight where valid
workflow.description: Compare responder profile to delivered-frame stats and target, track drop-off, and apply post-stratification weighting only on measured, covered axes with its limits
workflow.gate: the responder-vs-frame comparison and weighting-with-limits are stated as [ESTIMATE]s

workflow.action: Clear the FTC, sweepstakes, platform and privacy envelope
workflow.description: State FTC material-connection disclosure, the lottery test + No-Purchase-Necessary + AMOE + official rules + NY/FL registration, platform release/tagging rules, and privacy/consent/age-gate duties
workflow.gate: FTC disclosure, the AMOE-based lawful sweepstakes, platform rules and privacy/consent are all cleared

workflow.description: Apply the three joint conditions (cleared margin, bias-not-explaining-lead, on-target responders) and triangulate with S1/on-site data when the poll cannot clear the bar
workflow.gate: the three-condition gate and the triangulation fallback produce an explicit act/re-run/triangulate state

workflow.action: Tag honestly and hand off to assortment
workflow.description: Separate [FACT]/[ESTIMATE]/[UNKNOWN] via the honesty ledger and deliver the ranking as a caveated range + decision-state + bias caveats + responder profile + legal status, stopping before the SKU decision
workflow.gate: the caveated range, decision-state, bias caveats, profile and legal-clearance status are handed off without a market number or SKU choice

priority_rationale: The decision frame, target/frame/sample separation and total-survey-error budget come first because every bias claim and sample-size number is meaningless without the decision the poll serves, the population it is measured against, and the error framework that says which errors n can and cannot fix; the self-selection, platform, incentive, audience-mismatch and fraud nodes next, because they are the systematic biases that dominate an incentivized social poll; the sample-size, nonresponse, weighting, incentive-design and noisy-reading nodes then supply the [METHOD] to size, characterize, partially correct and honestly read the data; the FTC, sweepstakes, platform and privacy nodes establish the legal envelope the incentive must live inside; and the validity threshold, honesty ledger and hand-off come last because they compose the biases, reading and law into an act/re-run/triangulate decision and a caveated signal handed to the assortment stage without ever inventing a market number.

dominance_rules.rule: Bias direction dominates sample size in judging a poll
dominance_rules.rationale: self-selection, coverage and incentive bias are systematic offsets that a larger n cannot reduce
dominance_rules.trigger: a large response count is offered as proof the poll is reliable
dominance_rules.action: assess the coverage/nonresponse/incentive bias first; treat n as a floor to read a signal, not evidence of accuracy

dominance_rules.rule: Overlapping confidence intervals dominate a stakeholder's wish for a winner
dominance_rules.rationale: a within-margin lead is statistical noise, not a ranking
dominance_rules.trigger: the top categories' intervals overlap but a winner is wanted
dominance_rules.action: return 'no decision' and re-run or triangulate rather than declare a winner

dominance_rules.rule: Buyer-relevance of the incentive dominates raw response-lift
dominance_rules.rationale: a large sample of freebie-hunters answers the wrong question about the wrong people
dominance_rules.trigger: a bigger/generic prize is proposed to boost entries
dominance_rules.action: choose the buyer-relevant jewelry prize and buyer-targeted delivery, accepting lower raw response

dominance_rules.rationale: an illegal lottery, an FTC non-disclosure, or a platform breach can void the promotion and create liability
dominance_rules.trigger: a simple 'purchase/tag/share to win' mechanic is proposed
dominance_rules.action: build inside the envelope: No-Purchase-Necessary + AMOE + official rules + FTC disclosure + platform release + privacy consent

dominance_rules.rule: The bias-explanation test dominates a numeric margin alone
dominance_rules.rationale: a lead that the known bias direction could produce is not a real preference even if it clears the margin
dominance_rules.trigger: a lead clears the confidence interval on a biased sample
dominance_rules.action: require that the incentive/self-selection/coverage bias not plausibly explain the lead before acting

dominance_rules.rationale: weighting cannot recover zero-coverage groups or unmeasured self-selection
dominance_rules.trigger: a weighted result is presented as representative
dominance_rules.action: carry the weighting limits and treat the figure as a partial correction, never a representativeness certificate

dominance_rules.rule: The [UNKNOWN] register dominates the desire for a concrete number
dominance_rules.rationale: audience composition, lift, fraud rate and true preference are what the poll measures, not pre-known facts
dominance_rules.trigger: a concrete audience/lift/preference number is requested up front
dominance_rules.action: keep it in the [UNKNOWN]/[ESTIMATE] register with method until measured; never invent it as a fact

dominance_rules.rule: Triangulation dominates acting on a weak poll alone
dominance_rules.rationale: a single biased social poll is a weak basis for the launch set
dominance_rules.trigger: the validity gate returns re-run or the signal is bias-dominated
dominance_rules.action: combine with the S1 public-data demand read and existing on-site/bestseller data before acting

anti_rework_rules.rule: Clear the FTC/sweepstakes/platform/privacy envelope before launching the incentive, not after
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an illegal-lottery, non-disclosure or platform-takedown that voids the whole poll run and its data

anti_rework_rules.rule: Decide the minimum-signal n (with per-option cells) before running, not after collecting
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a finished poll whose thin per-option cells cannot separate the categories, forcing a full re-run

anti_rework_rules.rule: Design the incentive to be buyer-relevant and decoupled from the answer from the start
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a large freebie-hunter dataset about the wrong people that must be discarded and re-collected on-target

anti_rework_rules.rule: Set the responder-vs-target check and weighting axes before fielding, capturing the needed profile fields
anti_rework_rules.prevents: discovering post-hoc that the axes needed to assess or weight representativeness were never collected

anti_rework_rules.rule: Fix the overlapping-CI = no-decision reading rule before seeing the numbers
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a motivated post-hoc reading that declares a within-margin winner and drives a wrong launch set

anti_rework_rules.rule: Add deduplication, attention checks and eligibility screening to the entry flow up front
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a fraud-inflated sample discovered at analysis that must be cleaned or thrown out and re-run

anti_rework_rules.rule: Tag every figure [FACT]/[ESTIMATE]/[UNKNOWN] as it is produced
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an incentive-biased poll share circulating as a measured buyer preference that must later be retracted

anti_rework_rules.rule: Re-verify the live platform promotion guideline immediately before launch
anti_rework_rules.prevents: building an entry mechanic on a stale guideline that gets the promotion removed mid-run

iteration_protocol.trigger: an incentivized-vs-not A/B split measures the response-lift and bias skew
iteration_protocol.action: update the incentive-bias magnitude from [UNKNOWN] to an [ESTIMATE] and re-tune the incentive design levers

iteration_protocol.trigger: platform audience-insight stats for the delivered frame and the responder profile become available
iteration_protocol.action: estimate the coverage/nonresponse skew and apply valid weighting, then re-check the on-target-responders condition

iteration_protocol.trigger: more responses arrive or a day-over-day/segment replication is run
iteration_protocol.action: tighten the confidence intervals and re-apply the overlapping-CI reading rule and the validity gate

iteration_protocol.trigger: entry logs show duplicate/bot/geo-anomaly patterns or the prize value rises
iteration_protocol.action: strengthen the fraud controls, re-screen entries and re-estimate the residual fraud rate

iteration_protocol.trigger: the FTC, a state sweepstakes law, a platform promotion guideline, or a privacy regime changes
iteration_protocol.action: re-clear the compliance envelope and re-verify the affected [FACT-as-of] items before the next run

iteration_protocol.trigger: the validity gate returns re-run or triangulate
iteration_protocol.action: redesign the incentive/targeting for a cleaner poll or combine with S1 public-data and on-site data before acting

iteration_protocol.trigger: the launch-set decision or the target-audience definition the poll serves changes
iteration_protocol.action: re-fix the decision frame and the good-enough bar and re-propagate to the sample-size and validity nodes
